clue.text: What's primarily light and suitable at work?

definitions.text: What's primarily light and suitable at work?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of the word light, the first thing in it

parts.note: suitable means apt
OP, short for opus, is a work in music

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what is easy to carry and fit for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a light machine suitable at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable computer is light enough to carry and is made for office tasks, so the whole riddle describes one.

clue.text: Broadcasting perfect version of Wagner- N E er cycle

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or perfect; the figure 1 is read as the letter I
Wagner's cycle of four operas is The Ring; the stray letters are OCR noise on the page

explanation.surface: Someone praises a flawless broadcast performance of Wagner's operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Version of' is a link here. The OCR text carries stray marks after 'Wagner'; the clue reads 'Wagner's cycle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Airing a programme means putting it out on radio or television, the same as broadcasting it.

clue.text: Big servers whipped lobs past one

indicators.note: whipped, as cream is beaten up, signals that the letters of the next three words are mixed

explanation.surface: A tennis player's big serves are beaten as lobs fly past someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big servers' suggests tennis players, but it means large spoons for serving food.
explanation.definitionFit: These large spoons are used to serve food at table, so they are big servers.

clue.text: Religious group, finding holy book with power, see the light

parts.note: PI is crossword shorthand for pious, religious
a lot is a group or batch
Lam is the standard abbreviation for the biblical book of Lamentations
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A religious sect finds a sacred text with power and is converted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See the light' reads as a conversion; only 'light' defines, 'see the' leading to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small indicator bulb showing that equipment is switched on is a kind of light.

clue.text: Place leafy vegetable all round one type of fish

indicators.note: all round says the place and vegetable letters surround the letter for one

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
I is the Roman numeral for one
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A recipe: put the leafy greens around the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a verb telling the cook what to do, but it is the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This small oily sea fish, often tinned, is a kind of fish related to the sardine.

clue.text: Greek philosopher concerned with H Y E detail

parts.note: Plato was the Greek philosopher who wrote the Republic
on means about, concerned with

explanation.surface: A Greek thinker fusses over small particulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail' looks like small particulars, but in military use it is a squad assigned to a task. The OCR text has stray marks before 'detail'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the army a detail is a small group given a duty, as is a subdivision of a company.

clue.text: Dog failing to finish creamy drink

indicators.note: failing to finish says the dog's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Lassie is the famous collie of films and television

explanation.surface: A dog leaves a creamy drink half-done.
explanation.definitionFit: A lassi is an Indian yoghurt drink, thick and creamy.

clue.text: Witch uttered exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: uttered says the word is spoken, so its sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: heck is an exclamation of surprise; more than one are hecks

explanation.surface: A witch cries out in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a hex is a witch as well as the spell such a person casts.

clue.text: Gypsy dancer consumes one drink

indicators.note: consumes says the dancer's name swallows the letter for one

parts.note: Gypsy Rose Lee was a famous American burlesque dancer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Romany dancer downs a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gypsy' looks like a description of the dancer, but it is the first part of her name, Gypsy Rose Lee. ROSIE LEE is Cockney rhyming slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie Lee rhymes with tea in Cockney slang, so it means a cup of tea, a drink.

clue.text: Girl completely knocked over by a wild bear

indicators.note: wild says the letters of a bear are thrown into disorder
knocked over, in a down-to-across sense of toppling, says the word is turned backwards

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A girl is completely bowled over by a wild bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked over' reads as an attack by the bear; it signals reversal, and 'by' sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: In a way, former partner is a discriminating sort

indicators.note: In says the ex and is sit inside the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is described as discerning, in a way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discriminating' suggests discerning taste, but here it means prejudiced against one sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who discriminates on grounds of sex is a bigot of this kind.

clue.text: Lay siege wearing inappropriate clothing?

parts.note: in means wearing, as in dressed in
a vest, worn alone, is underclothing and unsuitable as outer dress

explanation.surface: Besieging soldiers turn up in unsuitable dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town is an old military term for surrounding it, laying siege.

clue.text: Here's drug — seizing it, perhaps impound?

definitions.text: Here's drug — seizing it, perhaps impound?

indicators.note: seizing says the rearranged word grabs and holds the drug letter inside
perhaps says the word impound is one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Police find drugs and wonder whether to impound them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges IMPOUND into OPIUMDN; 'seizing' sets E within it. The whole clue describes a place police might raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug den where opium is smoked is the place where drugs are, the place police would raid.

clue.text: Item for computer supplied by parents committee?

parts.note: a mother is one of a child's parents
a board is a committee that governs

explanation.surface: Parents' committee provides a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a school's parents' group donating equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: The main circuit board of a computer is a key item inside it.

clue.text: All the cops in newly-designed uniform? Wrong

indicators.note: newly-designed says the letters of the four words are reworked like a new pattern

explanation.surface: Every police officer turns out in a new uniform, but that is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a negation: what is the opposite of uniform? Not wearing one, as detectives do.
explanation.definitionFit: Police in ordinary dress rather than uniform are said to be in this, so it is the wrong answer to uniform.

clue.text: After Liberal joined with team, Labour leader secured convincing victory

indicators.note: After says the joining word and team follow the Liberal letter

parts.note: and joins one thing with another

indicators.note: secured says the team holds the leader's letter inside it

parts.note: a side is a team

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of the word Labour

explanation.surface: A political tale: a Liberal alliance helps Labour's leader win big.
explanation.walkthrough: The political surface is real election language; L goes inside SIDE to make SLIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is an election won by a huge margin, a convincing victory.

clue.text: Develop slowly as possible holiday destination in midwinter

indicators.note: in says the island goes inside the letters taken from winter

parts.note: midwinter is read literally as the heart of the six-letter word for the cold season
Cuba is a Caribbean island, one possible holiday destination

explanation.surface: Escaping winter to a sunny resort makes things grow slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midwinter' is read literally as the middle of the word itself, not the season; Cuba is a sunny winter escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To incubate is to let something develop gradually, as eggs or ideas do.

clue.text: Salary cut to inadequate amount, some may say … as result of this?

indicators.note: some may say signals that the phrase is a near match when spoken

parts.note: salary is income, and an inadequate amount is a pittance

explanation.surface: Pay reduced to a pittance, someone suggests, because of poor work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reaches back over the clue: a pay cut might be the result of being no good at the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inept at a job could lead to a salary cut, so this lack of ability is the cause.

clue.text: Old barman offers snifter, perhaps, pocketing coin

indicators.note: pocketing says the coin letter is put inside the small drink

parts.note: a snifter is a small drink, as is a taster
P stands for penny, a coin

explanation.surface: An old barman pours a small drink, pocketing a coin as a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster was a person who drew beer at an inn, an old word for a barman.

clue.text: Lavishly supply with drink? Right: for example, beer

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Offering plenty of drink, beer for example, seems right.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to entertain them lavishly with food and drink.

clue.text: Leave behind away team's garments

parts.note: out means away, not at home
a team's kit is its strip

explanation.surface: The visiting side leaves its kit behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip rivals is to go faster and leave them behind.

clue.text: From Ebro we rescued oarsman

indicators.note: From says the letters are taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: A rower is saved from the Spanish river Ebro.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ebro is a river in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower pulls an oar in a boat, so is an oarsman.

clue.text: Supply teacher prepared for small class?

parts.note: a supply teacher is a substitute teacher, a sub in British schools
set means prepared, ready

explanation.surface: A stand-in teacher is ready for a small class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like a school group, but in maths a subset is part of a set.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a subset is a smaller collection within a set, a small class.

clue.text: Care about providing container for a plant

indicators.note: providing container for says the turned word holds the letter A
about says the word for care is turned round

parts.note: care means worry, anxiety

explanation.surface: Someone frets about finding a pot for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns WORRY into YRROW; A goes inside after Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a flowering plant with feathery leaves, also called milfoil.

clue.text: Staff travelled endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rode means travelled, on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Staff journeyed on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a staff or stick.

clue.text: Sailing vessel shipshape, heading for Atlantic islands

parts.note: trim means neat, shipshape
the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland in the Atlantic

explanation.surface: A neat boat sets sail for islands in the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing boat with three hulls.

clue.text: Bidder is more sensitive

definitions.meaning: one who makes a bid or offer, as in a contract

explanation.surface: An auction bidder is touchier than others.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tenders is a bidder, and the comparative of tender means more sensitive.

clue.text: Chap cooks exotic vegetables

parts.note: Ed is a short man's name, a chap
does, as in does the dinner, means cooks

explanation.surface: A man prepares unusual vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddoes are taro corms, tropical root vegetables.
